'''Victor Gruschka Springer''' (June 2, 1928 – September 18, 2022) was an American biologist who was a Senior Scientist emeritus, Division of Fishes at the [[Smithsonian Institution]]'s [[National Museum of Natural History]].<ref name="affiliate">
{{Cite web
|url=http://www.si.edu/ofg/Staffhp/SpringerV.htm
|title=Victor G. Springer, Senior Scientist Emeritus
|date=21 October 2009
|access-date=7 December 2010
}} 
</ref>
He was a specialist in the anatomy, classification, and distribution of fishes, with a special interest in tropical marine shorefishes. He published numerous scientific studies on these subjects; also, a popular book called "Sharks in Question, the Smithsonian Answer Book" 1989.<ref>{{cite book 
|last1=Springer
|first1=Victor G.
|last2=Gold
|first2=Joy P.
|title= Sharks in Question
|date= April 17, 1989
|publisher= Smithsonian 
|isbn=978-0-87474-877-2 
}}</ref>

==Education==
Springer gained his first degree, B.A. in biology at [[Emory University]] in 1948. His M.S. in botany at the [[University of Miami]] in 1954 was followed by his Ph.D. in zoology at the [[University of Texas]] in 1957.<ref name="fishesstaff">
{{Cite web
|url=http://vertebrates.si.edu/fishes/fishes_staff_pages/springerv.cfm
|title=Vic Springer, Division of Fishes, Department of Vertebrate Zoology, NMNH
|access-date=7 December 2010
}}
</ref>

==Research interests==
Springer's research interests included the classification, evolution, and biogeography of fishes, especially marine fishes and notably [[:Category:Blenniidae|Blennioid fishes]]. He was also interested in late 19th and 20th Century scientific illustrators of fishes such as [[Charles Bradford Hudson]]<ref name="affiliate"/><ref name="fishesstaff" />

==Death==
Springer died on September 18, 2022, at the age of 94.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Victor Gruschka Springer (2 Jun 1928 – 18 Sep 2022) |url=https://www.asih.org/news |website=ASIH |access-date=20 November 2023 |date=19 September 2022}}</ref>

== Taxon named in his honor ==
*''[[Biwia springeri]]'' <small>([[Petre Mihai Bănărescu|Bănărescu]] & [[Teodor T. Nalbant|Nalbant]] 1973)</small> was named in honor of Springer who collected the type specimen.<ref name = ETYFish>{{cite web | url = http://www.etyfish.org/cypriniformes14/ | title = Order CYPRINIFORMES: Families ACHEILOGNATHIDAE, GOBIONIDAE and TANICHTHYIDAE | access-date = 3 March 2021 | author1 = Christopher Scharpf | author2 = Kenneth J. *The Springer's dragonet, '''''[[Synchiropus springeri]]''''' <small>[[Ronald Fricke|R. Fricke]], 1983</small> was named after him as it was he who collected the type specimens during his Fiji Islands Expedition in 1982 and loaned them and many other specimens to describer Fricke for examination.<ref name = ETYFish2>{{cite web | url = http://www.etyfish.org/syngnathiformes2/ | title = Order SYNGNATHIFORMES: Families DACTYLOPTERIDAE, PEGASIDAE, CALLIONYMIDAE, DRACONETTIDAE and MULLIDAE | access-date= 31 January 2023 | author1 = Christopher Scharpf | author2 = Kenneth J. Lazara | name-list-style = amp | work = The ETYFish Project Fish Name Etymology Database | publisher = Christopher Scharpf and Kenneth J. Lazara | date = 22 September 2018}}</ref>
*The '''Springer's barbelgoby''', '''''[[Gobiopsis springeri]]''''', is a [[species]] of [[goby]] found in the Western Central [[Pacific Ocean]].<ref name = ETYFish7>{{cite web | url = http://www.etyfish.org/gobiiformes5/ | title = Order GOBIIFORMES: Family GOBIIDAE (d-h) | access-date= 12 March 2023 | author1 = Christopher Scharpf | author2 = Kenneth J.
